stemMd: Treating insured-voyage counts as a direct measure of all voyages would require which assumption?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Insurance prices never affect any decision.

options.label: B
options.textMd: No ship ever made more than one voyage.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The proportion of voyages appearing in the insurance records did not change substantially.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Every trader used the same harbour.

options.label: E
options.textMd: All ships had the same cargo.

explanationMd: If recorded coverage changes, counts can rise without a matching rise in total activity. A stable recording proportion is therefore required for the direct proxy interpretation at issue.

distractorRationale.a: The necessary point is stable coverage, not a universal price claim.
distractorRationale.b: Counts can include repeated voyages consistently.
distractorRationale.e: Cargo equality is unnecessary for counting voyages.
distractorRationale.d: The issue is coverage within the studied port.
